beats.narration_slice: Seawater has too much salt for your body.
beats.visual: Full-bleed vertical linocut close-up of a bone-white drinking cup scooping turquoise seawater at the surf line, with dense rust-orange salt crystals exaggerated around the cup rim and suspended in the water to make the salt burden immediately visible.
beats.purpose: show that ocean water contains a salt load too high for normal hydration
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme close-up + cup dipping into foamy shoreline seawater + dense visible salt crystals + low waterline angle + diagonal surf composition
beats.continuity: begin inside the island world at the shoreline, immediately answering the freshwater problem without carrying over the opener composition

beats.narration_slice: Your kidneys use water to remove that salt.
beats.visual: Full-bleed simplified anatomical linocut cutaway of a human torso against an abstract indigo field, two kidneys prominent in bone white while translucent turquoise flow streams toward them and rust-orange salt particles funnel toward an outgoing urine stream.
beats.purpose: explain that kidneys require water to excrete excess salt
beats.visual_fingerprint: anatomical torso cutaway + paired kidneys + turquoise internal flow + orange salt particles exiting downward + centered frontal diagram composition
beats.continuity: shift from the salty drink to the body's internal mechanism responsible for removing that salt

beats.narration_slice: Drink seawater, and you may lose more water than you gain.
beats.visual: Full-bleed side-view survival figure kneeling on sun-bleached sand after drinking from a shell, with one small turquoise intake stream entering the body while a visibly larger turquoise outflow leaves toward the sand, surrounded by sparse rust-orange salt marks.
beats.purpose: show the net water-loss consequence of drinking seawater
beats.visual_fingerprint: side-view kneeling castaway + shell drinking vessel + small incoming water flow versus larger outgoing flow + dry beach setting + asymmetrical cause-and-effect composition
beats.continuity: translate the kidney mechanism back into a whole-body survival consequence and complete the opening promise payoff

beats.narration_slice: Rain can help if you collect it.
beats.visual: Full-bleed high-angle linocut of a sudden tropical rain shower striking broad palm leaves angled into an improvised bone-white container, turquoise rain channels converging into the vessel beneath softened storm-gray light.
beats.purpose: show rainwater as a usable freshwater source when actively captured
beats.visual_fingerprint: overhead rain catchment + slanted palm leaves + central collecting vessel + storm-gray shower + converging turquoise runoff geometry
beats.continuity: move from dangerous seawater to the first practical freshwater alternative

beats.narration_slice: Some islands have springs or fresh groundwater.
beats.visual: Full-bleed cutaway of a rocky island slope, with a clear turquoise spring emerging from shaded stone above while a second turquoise groundwater pocket sits beneath the sand and roots, both surrounded by carved indigo earth layers.
beats.purpose: show that some islands naturally contain springs or freshwater underground
beats.visual_fingerprint: island hillside cross-section + surface spring + underground freshwater lens + exposed roots and rock strata + split above-and-below composition
beats.continuity: expand the search for freshwater from weather-dependent rain to natural island water stores

beats.narration_slice: Others may have no reliable fresh water.
beats.visual: Full-bleed wide shot of a low barren coral islet under hard tropical sun, ringed by turquoise ocean but showing only cracked sand, dry palms and an empty tilted container casting a sharp shadow.
beats.purpose: show that some islands lack dependable freshwater sources despite being surrounded by water
beats.visual_fingerprint: very wide barren islet + empty container + cracked ground + harsh overhead sun + ocean encircling the dry land + sparse horizon-heavy composition
beats.continuity: contrast the water-bearing island cutaway with a separate island where those freshwater sources are absent

beats.narration_slice: Desalination can turn seawater into fresh water.
beats.visual: Full-bleed three-quarter view of a compact improvised desalination still on coastal rocks, seawater heating in one vessel as translucent vapor arcs through a cooling tube and condenses into clear turquoise drops in a separate clean cup.
beats.purpose: show the basic transformation of seawater into fresh water by desalination
beats.visual_fingerprint: three-quarter equipment view + heated seawater pot + curved vapor path + condenser tube + separate cup receiving clear drops + rocky shore workshop zone
beats.continuity: introduce a technological solution after showing an island with no reliable natural freshwater

beats.narration_slice: But it needs equipment, energy, and care.
beats.visual: Full-bleed low-angle still life of the desalination setup partially dismantled beside stacked fuel, a cracked hose, tools and a carefully tended flame, with hard shadows emphasizing the amount of supporting gear and maintenance involved.
beats.purpose: show that desalination depends on machinery, energy input and upkeep
beats.visual_fingerprint: low-angle maintenance still life + dismantled desalination parts + fuel bundle + tools + controlled flame + no human figure + dense foreground composition
beats.continuity: stay with desalination but change from successful output to the resources and maintenance required to keep it working

beats.narration_slice: Food, injury, disease, and aging still matter.
beats.visual: Full-bleed island shelter scene containing four integrated survival hazards without panels: an almost-empty food basket in the foreground, a bandaged ankle beside a walking stick, a feverish figure resting under shade with a water bowl nearby, and an elderly silhouette moving slowly near the shelter entrance.
beats.purpose: show that freshwater does not eliminate other major long-term survival limits
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium-wide shelter tableau + depleted food basket + bandaged limb + fever-resting survivor + elderly silhouette + layered foreground-to-background hazard composition
beats.continuity: pull outward from the desalination system to the wider set of survival pressures that remain even when water is available

beats.narration_slice: Even perfect fresh water cannot make island life last forever.
beats.visual: Full-bleed dusk linocut of a pristine vessel overflowing with clear turquoise fresh water in the foreground while an abandoned weathered shelter, spent food remnants and a long aging palm shadow recede toward a storm-gray horizon, the water abundant but the island visibly finite.
beats.purpose: close by showing that solving freshwater alone cannot remove every long-term limit on island survival
beats.visual_fingerprint: foreground overflowing freshwater vessel + distant weathered empty shelter + exhausted supplies + long dusk palm shadow + low horizon + reflective depth composition
beats.continuity: remain in the island world and resolve the preceding hazards into a quiet final image where water is plentiful but survival remains finite
